results.title: Two months ago the story was that datacenter GPU rental prices were holding flat while consumer cards slid. | Mercatus AI | The Open Intelligence Exchange
highlights:
Two months ago the story was that datacenter GPU rental prices were holding flat while consumer cards slid.

That flipped over the summer.

Cloud rental price per GPU-hour across 30+ providers, September 8:

B300 $8.89 (+5.7% since July 6)
AMD MI300X $4.99 (+6.4%)
H100 $3.85 (+4.6%)
H200 $4.54 (+3.7%)
B200 $6.42 (+1.7%)
A100 80GB $2.04 (flat)
RTX 5090 $0.70 (-1.4%)
RTX 4090 $0.49 (-2.0%)

Every current-generation datacenter GPU got more expensive to rent. The A100 held. Consumer cards kept slipping.

The spread is the point. The gap between an H100 and an RTX 4090 rental was $3.18/hr in July. It is $3.36/hr today. Capacity that can run production inference is getting pricier relative to capacity that cannot.

results.title: GPU Hour Pricing: A $3.44 Rate Cost $68.80 to Use | THE D*AI*LY BRIEF
highlights:
# GPU Hour Pricing: A $3.44 Rate Cost $68.80 to Use

Sixty-four B200s cost between $1.93M and $9.03M for a year depending only on how you buy them. But at the 5% GPU utilisation Cast AI measured across 23,000 production clusters, a committed $3.44/hr rate bills out at $68.80 per useful GPU-hour — and the break-even duty cycle is 48%.

...

Here is the verdict before the analysis. Buy on-demand from a neocloud until you can prove a duty cycle above roughly 50%, then commit — and never sign a commitment whose break-even utilisation is higher than the utilisation you have actually measured. For most enterprise AI teams that means Nebius or Together AI on the meter for the first two quarters, a 3-to-6-month committed rate after that, and spot reserved strictly for checkpointed training. Google Cloud's A4 is the loser on this table and it is not close: the highest list rate of the nine, and the only one you cannot buy on demand at all.

## What 64 B200s Cost for a Year, by How You Buy Them

Normalised to one workload for every row: 64 NVIDIA B200 GPUs — eight nodes of eight — held for twelve months. That is 560,640 GPU-hours at a 100% duty cycle. Same silicon, same node topology. The only variable is the purchasing instrument. All rates were read off each vendor's live pricing page, or a public price tracker where the vendor publishes none, on 8 September 2026.

| Purchase mode | Product | $/GPU-hr | 12 months, 64 GPUs | Break-even duty | Can you exit? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Committed term | CoreWeave Reserved (up to 60% off) | ~$3.44 | $1.93M | 40% | Contract term |
| Preemptible | Together AI preemptible B200 | $4.09 | $2.29M | Tolerates 50% waste | Instantly — against you |
| Reserved, 91–180d | Together AI Reserved Capacity | $6.79 | $3.81M | 83% | At term end |
| On-demand | Nebius HGX B200 | $7.15 | $4.01M | n/a | Hourly |
| On-demand | CoreWeave HGX B200 | $8.60 | $4.82M | n/a | Hourly |
| Reserved cluster | Lambda 1-Click Cluster, 64 GPU | $9.36 | $5.25M | n/a | 2-week minimum |
| Reserved block | AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks, p6-b200 | $12.36 | $6.93M | 87% | No — non-cancellable |
| On-demand | AWS p6-b200.48xlarge | $14.24 | $7.98M | n/a | Hourly |
| Reservation-only | Google Cloud A4 (a4-highgpu-8g) | $16.11 | $9.03M | n/a | No on-demand option |

Sources, in order. CoreWeave lists HGX B200 at $68.80 per 8-GPU node — $8.60 per GPU — and advertises Reserved Compute Capacity at "up to 60% discounts over On-Demand prices for committed usage"; $3.44 is that ceiling applied, and it is the only estimated figure in the table. Together AI publishes the rare public ladder: $8.19 on-demand, $7.99 at 7–30 days, $7.79 at 31–90 days, $6.79 at 91–180 days, and $4.09 preemptible. Nebius lists HGX B200 at $7.15 on-demand and $3.95 preemptible. Lambda charges $9.86 per GPU at 16 GPUs, $9.36 at 64 and $8.87 at 256+. AWS prices Capacity Blocks for p6-b200 at $12.355 per accelerator-hour, against an on-demand p6-b200.48xlarge rate of $113.933 per instance-hour, which is $14.242 per GPU. Google's a4-highgpu-8g carries eight B200s at roughly $16.11 per GPU-hour — an on-demand-equivalent rate, since Google publishes no on-demand price for the machine type.

The spread is 4.7x on identical hardware. None of it is a performance difference. Almost all of it is the difference between a rate card and a contract.

...

Take the floor literally against the table anyway, because it sets the scale of the risk. At a 5% duty cycle, those 64 GPUs do 28,032 hours of real work in a year. Buy them on the committed rate and you pay $1,928,602 for that work — $68.80 per useful GPU-hour, against a $3.44 line item on the invoice. Buy the identical 28,032 hours on Nebius's on-demand meter and you pay $200,429.

...

The published discounts are real and large: Together AI's preemptible B200 is $4.09 against $8.19 on-demand (50%), Nebius's is $3.95 against $7.15 (45%), CoreWeave's is $34.11 per node against $68.80 (50%), and AWS spot on p6-b200.48xlarge was $42.063 per instance-hour against $113.933 on-demand (63%). The useful way to read a spot discount is as a waste budget: at 50% off you can lose half of every job to preemption and still be level with on-demand.

...

It carries the highest list rate in the table at roughly $16.11 per GPU-hour — 2.25x Nebius for the same B200. And it cannot be launched on demand at all. Google's own documentation states that "when provisioning A4 machine types, you must reserve capacity to create instances or clusters, use Spot VMs, use Flex-start VMs, or create a resize request in a MIG," and for A4X (GB200) it is stricter still: "you must reserve capacity to create instances and clusters".

...

The GPU market has spent two years teaching buyers to think about scarcity, and scarcity thinking says: lock it in, lock it in long, take the discount. SemiAnalysis's index says that instinct is being priced — H100 one-year rental contracts rose from $1.70 to $2.35 per GPU-hour between October 2025 and March 2026, up almost 40% in five months. That is a term rate climbing into a shortage, not away from one: the same report has on-demand capacity sold out "despite recent price hikes," and spot bid up toward the on-demand rate. Signing a long commitment at the top of that curve locks in a peak, and committed capacity is the expensive end of the market for anyone who does not fill it.

...

It depends far more on how you buy than on what you buy. Checked 8 September 2026, an NVIDIA B200 runs $7.15/GPU-hour on-demand at Nebius, $8.60 at CoreWeave, $12.355 on AWS EC2 Capacity Blocks, $14.24 on AWS on-demand and about $16.11 on Google Cloud A4. Deep committed contracts reach roughly $3.44 and preemptible rates $3.95-$4.09. That is a 4.7x spread on identical silicon.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Compared 2026: What You're Really Paying For
highlights:
### Key Takeaways

- GPU cloud pricing for identical H100 hardware can vary roughly 5x between providers, from under $2/hr to nearly $7-12/hr.
- Whole-VM pricing (like some Google Cloud listings) and per-GPU pricing (like Lambda's) aren't directly comparable unless you normalize them first.
- Reserved capacity can cut on-demand rates by up to 60%, while spot/preemptible instances can be 60-91% cheaper but come with interruption risk.
- Dedicated GPU clouds like CoreWeave and Lambda typically run about half the cost of equivalent hyperscaler on-demand pricing.
- Hidden costs — egress fees, idle-node charges, minimum node sizes — often matter more to your final bill than the advertised hourly rate.
- The cheapest number on a pricing page is rarely the cheapest usable number once commitment terms and reliability are factored in.

...

GPU cloud pricing is the hourly, per-GPU, or capacity-block cost that cloud providers charge for renting access to specialized AI accelerators like Nvidia H100s, A100s, and B200s. Unlike standard cloud compute pricing, GPU pricing varies heavily by hardware generation, node configuration, networking quality, and commitment length, which is why the same chip can appear at wildly different prices depending on how and where you rent it.

...

Pricing Models

On-demand pricing costs the most but requires no commitment. Reserved capacity (typically 1-12 months) can cut costs by up to 60%. Spot/preemptible instances are cheapest but can be interrupted with little notice.

Tip: Match the model to the workload — spot for interruptible batch jobs, reserved for steady production traffic.

02

Hidden Costs

Egress fees for moving data out, minimum node sizes that force you to pay for GPUs you don't need, and idle-time billing can all add significant cost beyond the advertised hourly rate.

Tip: Ask for a full sample invoice, not just a rate card, before committing.

...

Before comparing quotes, convert every provider's price to a single normalized ... A "cheap" whole-VM price can hide multiple GPUs bundled together, making it look far more competitive than it actually is per accelerator.

...

| Category | Dedicated Clouds (CoreWeave, Lambda) | Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, GCP) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| On-Demand Cost | ★★★★☆ | ★★☆☆☆ | Dedicated clouds average roughly half of hyperscaler on-demand rates. |
| Pricing Transparency | ★★★★☆ | ★★★☆☆ | Fixed per-GPU pricing is easier to compare than Capacity Block or whole-VM pricing. |
| Enterprise SLAs / Compliance | ★★★☆☆ | ★★★★★ | Hyperscalers generally offer more mature enterprise certifications. |
| Best For | Cost-sensitive training and inference | Enterprise workloads needing broad compliance coverage | Both bill in USD, EUR, and GBP depending on region |

## Pricing: What GPU Clouds Really Cost in the US and Europe

The figures below reflect approximate 2026 on-demand rates for a single H100 GPU across the three major provider tiers. Actual pricing varies by region, node configuration, and availability — always confirm current rates directly with a provider.

| Dedicated Cloud (e.g. Lambda, CoreWeave) | $3.29-$6.16/hr | €3.03-€5.68/hr | £2.60-£4.87/hr |
| Hyperscaler On-Demand (e.g. AWS, Azure, GCP) | $4.72-$12.29/hr | €4.35-€11.33/hr | £3.73-£9.72/hr |

...

How much does an H100 GPU cost per hour in 2026?+

H100 rental rates in 2026 range from roughly $1.49/hr on budget marketplaces to over $12/hr on some hyperscaler on-demand listings, with dedicated GPU clouds typically falling in the $3-$6/hr range.

results.title: Jensen Huang Says a 22% Rent Jump Proves Old Nvidia Chips Keep Earning
highlights:
## Key takeaways

- Huang says a 22% jump in chip rental prices proves AI hardware keeps earning.
- The three-year-old Nvidia chip now rents for $3.28 an hour.
- The same chip once cost $7 to $8 an hour.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says rising AI chip rental prices prove that older hardware keeps earning, after rates for a three-year-old chip climbed 22% in a month.

The chip is the H100, the training processor behind the first wave of generative AI. It now rents for $3.28 an hour. Huang calls that durability. The longer record complicates the claim.

Index data circulated on X puts the hourly rate at $3.28, a gain of roughly 22% over the past month. Huang shared the chart and described Nvidia compute as fungible, durable, and revenue-generating.

...

The rebound cuts against standard accounting. Hyperscalers write down graphics processing units (GPUs) over roughly five to six years. Michael Burry argues the real useful life runs shorter, and he expanded his Nvidia short in late August.

## Why One Month Does Not Settle the Depreciation Debate

History cuts both ways here. On-demand capacity for the same chip once cost $7 to $8 an hour at large cloud providers, and early rates ran higher still. Against that base, $3.28 remains a steep markdown.

Supply also explains part of the move. Newer Blackwell systems stay reserved for the biggest buyers, so older clusters keep filling inference workloads. Tight power and memory keep the whole market expensive.

Then there is who pays the rent. CoreWeave, a cloud firm that buys Nvidia chips and rents them out, carried $35 billion of debt at the end of June. Nvidia, meanwhile, agreed to rent back unused capacity from such partners. Critics count that among the off-balance-sheet AI deals that flatter demand.

results.title: 晨涧云9月GPU算力资源及价格盘点：中端卡回血、高端卡略涨，这个月怎么租卡最划算 - 晨涧云AI算力平台
highlights:
晨涧云9月GPU算力盘点：11款显卡卡池、闲置率与卡时/天租/月租价格全解析。出口管制持续收紧下，A800、H100双双涨价，RTX 4080S、4090 24G、A100 40G库存紧张明显缓解。讲清高中低端显卡怎么选、计费方式怎么算最省钱。

...

2026年9月，晨涧云GPU算力租赁平台完成了新一轮显卡资源和价格盘点，涵盖当前上架的11款GPU型号、每种卡的卡池大小与闲置率，以及卡时、天租、月租三档计费方式的具体价格。跟8月比，这个月的变化不算小：中端卡的库存紧张情况普遍缓解，低端卡反而闲置卡变少了，价格方面除了A800、H100这两款顶级卡有小幅上调，其余型号基本按兵不动。这篇文章除了最新的表格，顺便聊聊这背后的市场逻辑，帮大家判断这个月该租哪张卡、用哪种计费方式更划算。

...

先说个背景。今年H100、A100这些数据中心级GPU对华出口受限的框架，其实从2022年就定下来了，中间几轮政策调整都没能真正打开缺口。今年1月，美国商务部工业与安全局把H200的审批方式从"推定拒绝"改成了"逐案审查"，看起来是松了一道口子，但据2月的报道，截至当时H200对华销售仍然是零，审批依旧停滞，不少中国客户干脆没敢下单。也就是说，H100、A100、以及英伟达专门为中国市场推出的"合规版"A800、H800，实际上都还压在这套限制框架里，没有实质性松动。

供给端收紧，价格自然扛得住。据SemiAnalysis的追踪数据，H100一年期租赁合约价格从2025年10月的1.70美元/GPU/小时，一路涨到2026年3月的2.35美元/GPU/小时，涨幅接近四成。国内渠道的报价也差不多同步往上走，多家平台的H100整机月租普遍落在8.5万到9万元这个区间，千卡级采购订单的交付周期更是拖到了2027年第一季度。

需求端也没闲着。行业里普遍的说法是，大模型应用全面落地之后，推理算力的消耗已经涨到训练算力的三到四倍。再加上不少传统行业的IT部门今年开始批量采购云算力，不再只是互联网公司和AI创业公司在唱独角戏，高端卡的需求曲线基本没有掉头的迹象。有意思的是，这轮涨价并不是雨露均沾：H100、A100、A800这类数据中心卡涨得最猛。

## 晨涧云9月GPU资源全景

完整的资源和价格表如下，一共11款显卡，覆盖从入门级到旗舰数据中心卡的全部区间。

| GPU | 卡池大小 | 闲置率 | 卡时价格（元） | 天租价格（元） | 月租价格（元） |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 3060 12G | ☆☆☆ | ☆☆ | 0.74 | 15 | 335 |
| RTX 2080Ti 22G | ☆ | ☆☆ | 0.88 | 18 | 448 |
| RTX 3080 20G | ☆☆☆ | ☆☆☆ | 0.98 | 20 | 499 |
| RTX 3090 24G | ☆☆☆☆☆ | ☆☆☆☆ | 1.22 | 25 | 650 |
| RTX 4080 Super 32G | ☆☆☆☆ | ☆☆☆ | 1.72 | 35 | 892 |
| RTX 4090 24G | ☆☆☆☆☆ | ☆☆☆ | 2.09 | 45 | 1050 |
| RTX 4090 48G | ☆☆☆☆ | ☆☆ | 3.19 | 65 | 1500 |
| A100 40G | ☆☆☆☆☆ | ☆☆☆☆ | 2.94 | 60 | 1499 |
| A100 64G | ☆ | ☆ | — | 85 | 2149 |
| A800 80G NVLink | ☆☆☆ | ☆☆ | — | 140 | 3696 |

两个星级栏容易看混，这里说清楚：

- 卡池大小是这个型号在平台上的总卡数，星星越多说明铺货越广；
- 闲置率是能立刻租到的空闲比例，星星越多说明越好租、不用排队抢。

...

## 这个月的变化：谁松了，谁更紧了

跟上个月的盘点比，最明显的变化出现在中端卡身上。晨涧云这个月上架了一批新机器，RTX 4080 Super 32G、RTX 4090 24G、A100 40G这三款的库存紧张情况都有实质性缓解——4080 Super的卡池从两星涨到四星，闲置率也跟着提了一档；4090 24G的卡池直接冲到五星；A100 40G的闲置率也肉眼可见地宽松了不少。这三款本来就是需求量最大的中端主力，这次补货算是解了不少用户的燃眉之急。

反倒是低端卡这边，这段时间闲置卡数量有点少，RTX 3060 12G的闲置率比上个月收紧了一档。而RTX 3080 20G、RTX 3090 24G这两款中低端卡的闲置率一直比较平稳，正常情况下都还能租到，不用太担心。

高端卡这边，紧张的老问题还是没解决，价格上还多了个新变化：A800 80G这次月租从上个月的3198元涨到3696元，涨幅约15.6%；日租也从130元涨到140元。同一时间，H100的月租也从8999元小幅上调到9999元，涨幅约11.1%。

值得一提的是，虽然显示RTX 4090 48G这类大显存消费卡没有明显恶化，但结合外部购买市场的行情看，这类卡的紧张程度其实一点没减。8月的市场数据显示，RTX 5090的外部售价已经涨到4万元以上，RTX 4090魔改48G也站上了2.5万元，两者都在持续上涨。原因也不复杂：本地部署大模型、多卡AI服务器、显存扩容需求这几年一直在增长，而RTX 4090核心已经停产，新增供给收缩得很明显——租赁需求本身就是被外部购买价格倒逼出来的。

顺带说一句市场里不太体面的现象：行业调研显示，不少平台标价看着便宜，用起来才发现带宽费、存储费另计，租户平均下来比标价多花两成五左右。晨涧云这次盘点里的价格，无论是卡时、天租还是月租，都是含CPU、内存、带宽的一口价，这一点对预算敏感的长租用户尤其重要——毕竟没人愿意签了合同才发现账单比预期高出一截。

...

三种计费方式选对了能省不少钱。按卡时价格连续租一个月（720小时）算一笔理论账，跟实际月租价格一对比就很清楚：

| GPU | 按卡时租满一月理论花费 | 实际月租价格 | 月租节省比例 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 3060 12G | 约533元 | 335元 | 约37.1% |
| RTX 3090 24G | 约878元 | 650元 | 约26.0% |
| RTX 4090 24G | 约1505元 | 1050元 | 约30.2% |
| RTX 4090 48G | 约2297元 | 1500元 | 约34.7% |
| A100 40G | 约2117元 | 1499元 | 约29.2% |

可以看到，只要用卡周期超过十天左右，月租基本都比按卡时零租划算，普遍能省下四分之一到三分之一的费用，显存越大的卡这个比例反而越高——RTX 4090 48G能省到近35%，比小显存的3090更划算。判断标准很简单：临时跑个实验、测环境，选卡时或天租，灵活不浪费；要连续跑训练、长期部署推理服务，或者项目周期确定在两周以上，月租肯定更省钱，还不用天天惦记续费。

...

总的来说，9月中端卡是最大的赢家——库存紧张普遍缓解，价格也没跟着涨；高端卡则是老问题加新压力，A800和H100双双上调价格，短期内很难指望缓解，出口管制这道坎不解决，这个局面大概率还会持续到今年底；低端卡虽然闲置率略有收紧，但价格依然是全表最低的一档，预算有限的用户不用太焦虑。

results.title: Nvidia H100-huurprijs stijgt 22 procent | FLOH Solutions
highlights:
Ornn ziet in zijn marktindex een maandgroei van ongeveer 19 tot 22 procent. Daardoor levert terugvallen naar oudere GPU's niet vanzelf een lagere AI-rekening op.

...

## Kort samengevat

- Ornn zette de H100 SXM in een grafiek op 3,28 dollar per GPU-uur, 0,59 dollar hoger dan een maand eerder.
- De eigen Ornn-marktpagina toont voor 7 september een settlement van 3,17 dollar en 19 procent groei in dertig dagen.
- Vraag naar inferentie, training en fine-tuning verschuift naar H100-capaciteit omdat nieuwere GPU's niet overal beschikbaar zijn.
- Een oudere GPU huren is daardoor niet meer vanzelf een besparingsstrategie; prijs en beschikbaarheid bewegen mee met de markt.

Nvidia H100-huurprijs stijgt in een maand met 21,89 procent naar 3,28 dollar per uur, meldt ChosunBiz op basis van Ornn, ondanks de komst van nieuwere AI-versnellers.

Voor een Nederlandse ondernemer die AI-inferentie afneemt, valt daarmee een bekende besparingsroute weg: een oudere GPU kiezen betekent niet automatisch een lagere rekening. De kostprijs van een productieomgeving hangt sterker af van beschikbare capaciteit en actuele vraag, juist wanneer de nieuwste kaarten niet genoeg leveren.

## De stijging is een richting, geen vast tarief

Ornn plaatste op 7 september een grafiek waarin de H100 SXM op 3,28 dollar per GPU-uur staat, 0,59 dollar boven de waarde van een maand eerder. Op de eigen marktpagina staat voor de settlement van die dag echter 3,17 dollar en een stijging van 19 procent in dertig dagen, vanaf 2,66 dollar.

Dat verschil komt door het meetmoment. De Ornn-index is een volumegewogen gemiddelde van uitgevoerde huurtransacties in een voortschrijdend uurvenster, geen vaste cloudprijs van één aanbieder. De richting is wel hetzelfde: de H100-index staat hoger dan een maand eerder, maar de dagbewegingen zijn stevig. De index is daarom een signaal van prijsdruk, geen universele offerte voor elke Nederlandse cloudrekening.

...

De H100 komt uit 2022, maar blijft bruikbaar voor AI-training en inferentie. Nvidia beschrijft de kaart zelf als een datacenter-GPU voor grootschalige training en inferentie, met 80 GB HBM3-geheugen. ChosunBiz schrijft dat de vraag naar real-time inferentie, training van kleine en middelgrote modellen en fine-tuning naar de H100 verschuift, omdat het aanbod van nieuwere Blackwell- en Rubin-versnellers de vraag niet volledig opvangt.

Ornn-grafiek toont de H100 SXM-index op 3,28 dollar per uur en 21,89 procent groei in een maand, bron: Ornn via X

Een taak hoeft dus niet de nieuwste kaart nodig te hebben om toch capaciteit op te eisen. De H100 is breed geplaatst, de software eromheen is volwassen en aanbieders kunnen bestaande capaciteit opnieuw inzetten voor productiegebruik. Daardoor werkt ouder worden hier niet automatisch als prijsmechanisme.

De verhouding met nieuwere kaarten laat zien waarom de oude generatie aantrekkelijk blijft. In dezelfde Ornn-snapshot staat de H200 op 4,56 dollar per uur en de B200 op 6,75 dollar. De H100 kost daarmee ongeveer 72 procent van de H200-prijs en bijna de helft van de B200-prijs. Dat is nog steeds een verschil, maar het maakt de H100 niet goedkoop in absolute zin.

...

Het eerdere CoreWeave-signaal zat op contractniveau: CoreWeave verhoogde in juli de tarieven met ongeveer 25 procent en meldde dat ook oudere GPU-capaciteit voor de korte termijn uitverkocht was. De Ornn-index laat nu zien hoe zo'n verschuiving ook buiten één verhuurder zichtbaar wordt.

De index zegt niet dat elk contract morgen duurder wordt. Ornn meet alleen on-demand transacties; gereserveerde capaciteit en langlopende contracten vallen buiten de index. Voor een afnemer maakt dat onderscheid uit: een lopend meerjarig contract kan dezelfde prijs houden, terwijl een nieuwe productieomgeving direct met schaarse en beweeglijke tarieven te maken krijgt.

results.title: Nvidia DGX Cloud pricing: why there’s no rate card, and what replaced it | AI Compute Marketplace | Compare GPU Cloud & Data Centers | ComputeStacker Insights
highlights:
There has never been an official rate card for NVIDIA DGX Cloud. The only price revealed by NVIDIA at launch was $36,999 per instance per month, which occurred in 2023.

Currently, it is only possible to get pricing through a private request from a partner or directly from the cloud providers. No price list is available to refer to.

This is not by mistake, but simply because of the way NVIDIA sells this product. This is also because of the new strategy adopted by Nvidia, making pricing even less transparent than before.

...

- There has never been an official rate card for Nvidia’s DGX Cloud. The only figure released by Nvidia was $36,999 per instance per month, which came during the 2023 launch of DGX Cloud.
- Currently, the only way to get a proper price quote is through private pricing through a partner or by comparing cloud services.
- As of the end of 2025, Nvidia is no longer marketing DGX Cloud to new external customers. Most of its capacity is now being used internally.
- The alternative that Nvidia is directing its customers towards is called DGX Cloud Lepton, which is a GPU marketplace model. It does not have an official rate card either.
- The rollout of DGX Cloud took longer than Nvidia had planned. AWS joined the effort about two and a half years after the initial launch date.
- Nvidia charges for DGX Cloud using a subscription-per-node pricing model.

...

Nvidia’s DGX Cloud-specific terms of service clearly state the billing structure: subscription-based per node. However, they provide no information regarding subscription costs.

The only publicly disclosed pricing for DGX Cloud was the launch pricing itself. In March 2023, Nvidia’s press release announced the launch of DGX Cloud clusters at a price of $36,999 per instance per month.

That was over two years ago. Nvidia has maintained the same pricing since then.

## Is there a DGX Cloud price per GPU or per H100?

Not at all. And that confuses many readers. DGX Cloud is not available on an itemised basis as a rental for individual GPUs.

The pricing is for managed nodes or clusters. The term “node” includes the hardware, networking, and Nvidia software together as one product, not as individual components.

As a result, there is no officially released figure for “$X per H100 per hour” for DGX Cloud. All such figures floating around lack a verifiable Nvidia source. Therefore, approach them with caution.

If what you are looking for is the per-GPU hourly price, then that’s another product line entirely.

...

And here’s the relevant excerpt from above. Nvidia has been quietly pivoting away from DGX Cloud as a customer-facing product.

As reported by both Tom’s Hardware and DataCenterDynamics, this pullback took place between September and December 2025. In both cases, sourcing has come from The Information. Nvidia apparently ended any sales pitches for DGX Cloud with outside customers.

Apparently, Nvidia reassigned the vast majority of Nvidia’s DGX Cloud capacity to internal research and development work. The company also integrated the DGX Cloud team into Nvidia’s internal engineering division.

But note that this information comes from reporting, not from a statement on record from Nvidia. However, several sources have confirmed this information, not just one.

There’s a fairly obvious answer to why this was done. In 2023, when DGX Cloud launched, GPU capacity was scarce, and hyperscalers were expensive. However, by 2025, hyperscalers had lowered their GPU pricing dramatically.

...

DGX Cloud is Nvidia’s original managed AI supercomputing service delivered via hyperscaler partners. DGX Cloud was, as mentioned above, being phased out for new customers.

DGX Cloud Lepton is a more recent service offering, which isn’t a similar offering to the previous one. It is a marketplace that links buyers and Nvidia Cloud Partners (NCPs) directly.

| Category | DGX Cloud | DGX Cloud Lepton |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | Managed AI supercomputing service | GPU marketplace connecting buyers to NCPs |
| Sold through | Hyperscaler partners (AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI) | Direct marketplace access |
| Current status | Being wound down for new customers | Active, the current path forward |
| Published rate card | None | None |

...

There isn’t any officially published information about a rate per GPU for DGX Cloud. Nvidia markets its DGX Cloud service as a node or cluster subscription, rather than as individual GPUs.

# Jensen Huang shared Ornn data, and the rental price for H100 increased by 22% in one month 

 2026-09-08 11:23:42 

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang shared data from the computing power market Ornn. Ornn stated that the H100 has been a training GPU for several years, but the rental price has increased by 22% in the past month, now reaching $3.28 per hour per unit. Jensen Huang emphasized that NVIDIA's computing power can continuously generate rental income, making it a revenue-generating asset.

Ornn's H100 index is calculated based on actual rental transaction prices. The daily settlement price on September 7 was $3.17 per hour, and the latest displayed price further rose to $3.28. NVIDIA stated in its latest earnings report that GPUs can be redeployed across different customers and workloads.

# NVIDIA H100 GPU Rental Prices Rise 22% in Past Month to $3.28 per Hour

2026-09-08 03:26:15

According to Ornn data shared by NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang on September 7, H100 GPU rental prices rose 22% over the past month to $3.28 per hour. The data is calculated from actual leasing transaction prices on Ornn's H100 index.

Huang highlighted that GPUs can generate recurring rental income and be redeployed across different clients and workloads, reinforcing NVIDIA's position that compute infrastructure serves as a revenue-generating asset.
